cim: IBM Quantum's Joseph Broz To Keynote Next Edge Alliance Launch
cim_eredeti: IBM Quantum's Joseph Broz To Keynote Next Edge Alliance Launch
szoveg_eredeti:
Dr. Joseph Broz, Vice President at IBM Quantum, will keynote the November 3 launch of the Next Edge Alliance, an impact investing exchange holding its event at the Ford Center at The Star in Frisco, the Dallas Cowboys’ world headquarters. The Alliance’s platform, Investor Hive, trains its AI on the collective investment insights of its founding members, rather than open web data.

“When capital is aligned with mission, it becomes more than an investment. It becomes a way to make a difference,” says Co-Founder and CEO Andréa Albright, as the event aims to broaden access to private market opportunities.

Dr. Broz’s presentation will detail how advancements in quantum technology are reshaping security protocols relevant to financial markets and private equity. The Next Edge Alliance’s platform, Investor Hive, employs a unique approach to artificial intelligence, training its system on the judgment, decision history and pattern recognition of the Alliance’s founding investors, the company says.

This proprietary training methodology suggests a highly selective and potentially exclusive investment analysis process, prioritizing insights from experienced investors over open-source information. The event’s core philosophy is encapsulated in the statement, “One day. One room.” The launch event is designed for accredited investors, family offices and individuals facilitating connections within the impact investing space, and the Alliance intends to shift the paradigm of capital allocation, aligning financial returns with measurable social and environmental impact.

When capital is aligned with mission, it becomes more than an investment. It becomes a way to make a difference.

Source: https://www.einpresswire.com/article/952385510/next-edge-alliance-to-launch-at-the-star-in-frisco-with-ibm-quantum-keynote

Where classical computers manipulate bits that are either on or off, quantum machines exploit superposition and entanglement to process information in ways that classical physics cannot. Dr. Donovan tracks the full quantum landscape: fault-tolerant computing, photonic and superconducting architectures, post-quantum cryptography, and the geopolitical race between nations and corporations to achieve quantum advantage. The decisions being made now, in research labs and government offices around the world, will determine who controls the most powerful computers ever built.
